observation_summary: The binomialCoefficient method was failing for large inputs due to precision issues caused by using floating-point arithmetic (Math.round(binomialCoefficientDouble(n, k))) to calculate values that should be exact long integers.
reasoning_summary: The fix replaces an incorrect computational strategy (relying on floating-point approximation via binomialCoefficientDouble) with a robust, iterative integer-based algorithm that handles potential overflows and intermediate precision issues using GCD-based division and overflow-checked multiplication. This is a fundamental change to the computational procedure, fitting the Algorithm/Method definition.
evidence_used: The fix replaces the line 'long result = Math.round(binomialCoefficientDouble(n, k));' with a multi-branch iterative loop structure.
The fix introduces explicit logic for different ranges of n (n <= 61, n <= 66, and n > 66) to manage overflow and precision.
The bug report explicitly mentions that the failure is due to rounding errors in the existing implementation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not merely changing a constant or initialization value; it is replacing the entire computational approach for calculating the binomial coefficient.
While the fix adds checks for overflow and range, these are part of the new algorithmic implementation to ensure correctness, not just missing guards for existing logic.
